title: Getting started
text: Getting started 1. Click Editor (or "Start writing") — a fresh project is created instantly in your browser. 2. Type Markdown; mix in math Inline LaTeX e^{i pi} = 1 Display equations int_a^b f(x) ,dx AsciiMath shorthand a/b 3. Press and a letter to search 100+ math commands with live previews. 4. Organize with folders in the left tree; create chapters with + . 5. Export switch the preview to PDF (compiled by Typst) or use print . Everything autosaves ~2 seconds after you stop typing, and again when you close the tab.

title: How it works
text: How it works keystroke → CodeMirror → zustand store ─┬→ KaTeX fast preview (250ms debounce) ├→ IndexedDB autosave (2s idle) └→ compiler worker → Typst WASM → PDF blob The page shell is static HTML; one client island owns everything. A generation counter drops stale compile results so typing never lags. The Typst engine runs in a nested worker (JSPI when available); wasm + fonts load once from static assets. Dexie (IndexedDB) is the source of truth — the store is just a cache.

title: What is xtype
text: What is xtype xtype is a local first editor for math heavy writing . Everything — editing, math rendering, even PDF compilation via Typst/WebAssembly — happens inside your browser. Documents persist in IndexedDB on your device. Zero server compute no accounts, no uploads, no timeouts Instant KaTeX preview while you type Publication grade PDF export via the Typst compiler running in a web worker Start with [Getting started](/docs/getting started), or jump straight into [syntax basics](/docs/writing/basics).

title: Syntax basics
text: Syntax basics xtype documents are Markdown with three math modes Syntax Meaning ... Inline LaTeX math ... Display (block) math ... AsciiMath converted to LaTeX Markdown features supported headings , bold , italic , inline code, code fences, lists, blockquotes, links. For the full list of math commands see the [command reference](/docs/writing/commands).

title: AsciiMath
text: AsciiMath Prefer plain text math? Wrap it in double colons and it converts to proper typeset math a/b → fraction sum_(i=1)^n i^3 → summation oo → infinity AsciiMath is great for quick notes; switch to LaTeX ( ... ) when you need fine control.
